Your bore was fine yesterday. Today it won't let go.
Some clays swell the moment they touch water. They absorb it, expand, and squeeze tight around the rods.

That's reactive ground. It doesn't matter how good your mud is if the formation itself is closing in on you.

Winter makes it worse. More moisture in the ground means more swelling before you even start pumping fluid.

The fix isn't more mud weight. It's stopping the clay from absorbing water in the first place. You need something in the fluid that gets to the clay face before the water does.

Block the absorption and the bore stays open.
What ground gives you the most trouble in winter?

Clay Control stops reactive ground from grabbing your rods.
It works by coating the clay face before water gets in. The clay can't swell if it can't absorb.

Mix it into your fluid program from the start. Trying to fix a swollen bore after the fact is a losing game.

Works across HDD, water well, and geotech. Any ground with reactive clays, Clay Control earns its place in the tank.

Heading into winter, keep a few bags on the truck. When the ground changes, you're already set.
Running Clay Control on your winter jobs? Talk to the team about dialling in the right rate for your ground.
